facts.raw_span: A 69-year-old woman
history of hypertension
stage IA estrogen receptor–positive and progesterone receptor–positive and ERBB/neu receptor–negative invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast
presented with blurry vision in both eyes
1 mg of anastrozole daily 6 months prior to her presentation
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/40 OD and 20/25 OS
Pupils were equal, round, and reactive without an afferent pupillary defect
Intraocular pressures were normal
mild cataracts in both eyes
parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in the right and left eyes
the crystalline deposits did not display autofluorescence
Crystalline deposits located at the level of the outer plexiform layers with some extension into the inner nuclear area subfoveally

concepts.why: The patient's history of anastrozole use and the presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes, which did not display autofluorescence, suggest anastrozole-induced crystalline maculopathy.
The patient's age and the presence of mild cataracts in both eyes support the diagnosis of age-related cataract.
The patient's history of hypertension and the presence of blurry vision in both eyes suggest hypertension-related retinopathy.
The patient's history of breast cancer treatment with anastrozole and the presence of crystalline deposits in both eyes suggest breast cancer treatment-related ocular toxicity.
It explains the finding of reduced best-corrected visual acuity in the context of crystalline deposits in the retina.

rationales.F05: Anastrozole use is a known risk factor for crystalline maculopathy
rationales.F10: Parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits are characteristic of crystalline maculopathy
rationales.F12: Crystalline deposits at the level of the outer plexiform layers are consistent with crystalline maculopathy

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of parafoveal shimmering golden crystalline deposits in both eyes, which did not display autofluorescence, and the patient's recent initiation of anastrozole, strongly supports Anastrozole-induced crystalline maculopathy as the most specific diagnosis.
